identity.name: Sodium citrates
identity.chemical_class: Sodium salts of citric acid (citrate salts)

function.mechanism: Acts as a citrate buffer system to control pH and as a metal-ion complexing agent that can improve formulation stability.
common_food_categories: beverages and formulations using citrate buffering

adi.basis: OpenEFSA records for E331(i)-(iii) show ongoing risk assessment with no published final output/ADI yet (last modified 2026-01-19).

efsa.key_finding: E331 is already authorised in the EU; re-evaluation is ongoing and delayed, with a new call for data planned in 2026.

concerns.summary: A mouse postweaning exposure study reported long-lasting, sex-dependent social-behavior effects with associated biological changes after sodium citrate exposure in drinking water.
Human high-dose supplementation studies report gastrointestinal symptom burden in performance/supplement contexts; this is above typical food-additive exposure context.

Because E331 contributes sodium, high total sodium dietary patterns may be a contextual concern in sodium-restricted individuals, though additive-specific harm evidence was not strong in retrieved sources.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA sodium citrate entries report ADI not limited/not specified and state no significant toxicological hazard for citric acid and its sodium salts in evaluated use contexts.
FDA affirms sodium citrate as GRAS in 21 CFR 184.1751 with GMP-based use conditions.
No IARC agent listing was found for sodium citrate in the current IARC classifications dataset reviewed.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric EFSA or JECFA ADI value was available to compute exceedance; JECFA ADI is not specified/not limited.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence remains permissive (FDA GRAS; JECFA ADI not specified/not limited; no IARC listing), while EFSA re-evaluation is still ongoing and some recent animal/high-dose human studies justify continued monitoring rather than a risk-free classification.
key_factors: FDA 21 CFR 184.1751 GRAS with GMP use condition
JECFA ADI not limited/not specified for sodium citrate entries
No IARC classification found for sodium citrate
EFSA re-evaluation records are ongoing with no current final output
Recent animal and supplementation studies show context-specific effects
